Definition: from G5257; to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication) subserve:--minister (unto), serve.
BiblicalUsage: The word hypēretéō carries the sense of to serve, to minister, to attend. In Acts 13:36, the text says "after he had served his own generation by the will of God." In Acts 20:34, the text says "that these hands have ministered unto my necessities."
TheologicalSignificance: I take hypēretéō to mean that serving is not earning; it is answering love with love. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Paul's Missionary Journeys; Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa; Paul Preaches at Pisidian Antioch
